title: Rochdale care leaver behind Little Acts of Christmas explains why no young person should go without a gift
excerpt: Brianna, who grew up in care, started Little Acts of Christmas to give presents to young people in care. Her appeal has passed £900, with more than 30 requests so far.
body:
A young Rochdale care leaver has explained why she started Little Acts of Christmas, an independent appeal to make sure children and teenagers in care do not go without a present this Christmas.

Brianna, who grew up in the care system herself, set up the project to provide gifts for young people aged roughly 10 to 18 who are in care, care-experienced or otherwise at risk of missing out. She runs it alone, without a charity, staff or budget behind her, and has built it largely through TikTok alongside a GoFundMe page and an Amazon wishlist.

In a statement supplied to Rochdale Daily, Brianna said: "Christmas is often portrayed as a magical time of year, but for some children and young people, it can be a reminder of the things they don't have, the people they might be missing or the difficult circumstances they're growing up in."

She added: "I didn't want to just sit back and accept that some young people might go without Christmas presents or that they might feel forgotten. Instead, I wanted to do something about it."

Brianna said young people in care, and those leaving it, can feel increasingly overlooked as they get older, and that she wanted to turn her own experience into something positive for others.

"I'm not a big organisation, I don't have a team of employees or a large budget behind me. I'm simply someone who understands how important even the smallest act of kindness can be," she said.

The appeal set out to raise £800 to buy gifts for more than 50 young people. On 2 November it stood at £140, with more than 12 young people having already messaged Brianna through TikTok to ask whether they could receive a present.

Since then the total has risen sharply. Brianna told Rochdale Daily that the appeal had passed £900 by Saturday 7 November, including a £700 donation from a business whose owner is himself a former care leaver.

Requests have grown too, to more than 30. Brianna said she has paused new requests until Thursday 12 November so that she does not promise gifts she cannot deliver. She plans to go shopping that day for the 30 young people already on her list, and will reopen requests if enough money remains.

She also has to cover postage, as she wants the project to reach young people beyond Rochdale.

Brianna is asking for financial donations, brand-new gifts, support from local businesses and organisations, or simply for people to share the fundraiser. She hopes to grow Little Acts of Christmas into a larger initiative across Greater Manchester and beyond, possibly as an independent organisation in future.

"A present might seem like a small thing to some people, but to someone who isn't expecting anything, knowing that somebody has thought about them can mean so much more than the gift itself," she said.

Donations can be made through the Little Acts of Christmas GoFundMe page at gofund.me/be1e51022, and the project can be found on TikTok at @Littleactsofchristmas.

Have you been helped by a project like this, or could your business support the appeal? Let us know in the comments.

Source: Statement and fundraising update from Brianna, founder of Little Acts of Christmas, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Image: Little Acts of Christmas logo, supplied.
